reasoning: Genuine version differs from the planted control only in the three date fields (both clause first_end dates and whole_order_end now 1968-04-25). Re-checked on the same standard: all cited text hashes and quote spans match; PDF sha256 values match the jobs/fr-originals manifest. Identity confirmed (EO 8399, April 29, 1940, Franklin D. Roosevelt, 5 FR 1607, filed 1940-04-30). The two-clause inventory (the lead folded into permission (1); permission (2)) covers the whole operative text. EO 11408 (33 FR 6459, signed and filed April 25, 1968, no effective-date provision) sec. 1 revokes EO 9 of 1873 and sec. 2 revokes all prior orders 'insofar as they interpret or amend Executive Order No. 9', listing 8399; the claim's dates, actor (EO:11408), mechanism (express revocation) and whole-order end (= latest clause end) now agree with the source and with its own later_events and prose. OFR note 'Revoked by: EO 11408, April 25, 1968 (in part)': in the blind review I listed its unnamed '(in part)' qualifier as a secondary defect; on reconsideration the claim resolves it on the merits (the order is wholly an amendment of EO 9 and each clause is an exception to the revoked prohibition, so sec. 2 reaches all of it, and sec. 1 removed the prohibition itself), which is the correct reading; not a defect. Earlier-end test: cruden number search finds no held text citing EO 8399 by number; I read the other held EO 9 amendments of 1940-1955 (EO 8516, 8880, 9442, 9845, 10044, 10055, 10645): none revokes, restates or supersedes EO 8399 (EO 8516 suspends the prohibition for defence posts, which does not end these exceptions). No held text documents the 1946 abolition of the Social Security Board (grep of APP and FR texts finds only pre-1946 orders); the claim discloses it and does not rely on it, the same standard applied to the upheld claims for EO 11299, 11409, 11468 and 11499. Savings correct (EO 11408 has no savings clause). Searches adequate and honestly described.
